newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Guilder rates languish in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Guilder rates languish in thin trade.

text.p: Guilder rates held steady in thin trade on Tuesday as the money market languished in the absence of any new cues on direction.
Dealers said London's reopening after the bank holiday weekend had failed to kickstart the Dutch market and volumes remained low.
"There has been some action in one- and two-month guilder deposits, but nothing really spectacular," one said.
Overnight guilders were unchanged at 2.62 percent bid, as were one- and two-month guilders at 2.74 and 2.78 percent bid respectively.

Dealers said this month's auction of Netherlands Bank Certificates (NBCs) had held no surprises, with the yield being fixed at 2.90 percent, 10 basis points below Tuesday's equivalent (six-month) Amsterdam interbank offered rate.
The Dutch central bank reported total bids of 3.76 million guilders, of which 2.0 million guilders were accepted to take the allotment on yield to 45.0 percent.

Prices at the longer end of the money market curve were also virtually unchanged from Monday. Three-month guilders quoted at 2.82 percent bid, while one-year deposits were quoting up two basis points at 3.16 percent bid.
The guilder was quoted at 112.10 per 100 marks, down fractionally from Monday's mid-afternoon quote of 112.09.
